Given some static vector, of formants, the NN could make a decision about
a few possible categories… Problem: Human cognition is far more complex…

speakerNotes: Fully connected neural network: 2 inputs, hidden layers of 3, 2, and 4 neurons, and 5 outputs. Right arrow reveals all 40 illustrative signed weights. The weights are fixed across both slides.

shapes.text:
1985: Michael Jordan developed Recurrent Neural Networks to make
sense of speech production…. which became LLMs… then Agentic AI ☺️

LLM: dynamical system with
many vectors in, 1 decision vector out

Agentic system:
a graph of LLMs

Inference: inner products
Learning: SGD + DP

speakerNotes:
Click 1: one neuron — a vector comes in, one number comes out (an inner product).
Click 2: a small network, layers 4-3-4-5 — each W turns a vector into a vector; the last layer is a decision vector.
Click 3: an LLM — 15 token vectors go in at the bottom, pass up through 5 layers of W's (6 colours = 6 kinds of W), and the top yields vector 16: a probability distribution over the next token.
Click 4: agentic systems — several LLMs wired into a graph, with a critic/revise loop.
Click 5: the two operations under everything: inference is inner products; learning is SGD plus dynamic programming (backprop).

shapes.text: The cat that the dog chased ran up the old tree and sat on the ____
an image, cut into 16 patches, read row by row
a protein (insulin, B chain), read as 15 amino acids
The LLM only ever sees vectors. Words, sounds, pixels, molecules: one machine, one question: what is x₁₆?

speakerNotes:
Start: just 15 vectors and an empty 16th slot. Ask: vectors of what?
Click 1: a sentence, cut into 15 words; each x_i points at one word. x_16 is the missing word.
Click 2: the words go; now a spectrogram, cut into 15 frames. Same x_i, now pointing at frames. x_16 is the next frame.
Click 3: now an image cut into 16 patches, read row by row. x_16 is the missing bottom-right patch.
Click 4: now a folded protein (insulin B chain, FVNQHLCGSHLVEAL) read as a sequence of amino acids. x_16 is the next residue (it is Y).
Click 5: the takeaway: the machine only sees vectors; the sequence can come from anywhere.

shapes.text: Which sequences can be English words?
A simple syllable in English can have a consonant then a vowel then a consonant
Only certain sequences are allowed before the vowel and after the vowel
A long word is a chain of syllables: t·l is fine across a break (At·lan·tic), but tl cannot start a syllable

speakerNotes:
Click 1: twenty one-syllable words, each a single consonant, a single vowel, a single consonant (consonants dark, vowel red, silent e grey).
Click 2: the CVC rule.
Click 3: clusters. Top: real words with clusters (blue). Bottom: an impossible twin (red, starred). Many twins use the same letters in the other order (flat/*lfat, help/*hepl, lamp/*lapm): order matters, and it mirrors around the vowel.
Click 4: only certain sequences are allowed before and after the vowel.
Click 5: many-syllable words. Atlantic, athlete, admit contain t-l, th-l, d-m, which are impossible as onsets (*tlantic, *thlete, *dmit) but fine across a syllable break. ng can end a syllable (ring) but never start one (*ngapkin).
Click 6: a word is a chain of syllables, each obeying the same rules.

shapes.text: How phonotactic knowledge can be revealed through GPT learning
Each is the start of an English word. Guess the next letter.
l r a e i o
l, r or a vowel    never *spn
r l a e i o u
r, l or a vowel    never *bn
r l a e i o u
r, l or a vowel    never *fn
a e i o u r
Guessing the next letter is predicting x₁₆. A GPT trained only on this game learns English sounds and spelling.

speakerNotes:
Let students guess first. Notice how fast they agree, and how the agreement changes from item to item.
Click 1: likely next letters (green), the rule, and one impossible continuation (red).
  The contrast to draw out: after a vowel (fa_) almost anything can follow; at the start of a word the choices narrow sharply (sp_, b_, f_: r, l or a vowel), and after skr_ or m_ only a vowel is possible.
  bram_ almost forces b (bramble), but a new syllable could also start there.
Click 2: guessing the next letter is exactly the next-token game. A GPT that only ever plays it learns these patterns: its predicted distribution is flat after fa_ and sharply peaked after skr_.
